observation_summary: The `Selector` class fails to parse complex CSS selectors containing attribute regexes when preceded by a combinator. hypothesis: The `combinator` method in `Selector.java` uses `tq.consumeToAny(combinators)` to parse the sub-query. This method is too simplistic because it does not account for nested structures (like attribute selectors `[...]` or pseudo-selectors `(...)`) that might contain characters present in the `combinators` set.
prediction: The `combinator` method will be shown to be using a naive `consumeToAny` call that fails to handle the `[class~=x|y]` part of the query because the `|` or other characters might be misinterpreted or the parser simply stops too early, leaving the rest of the string to cause a `SelectorParseException`.
